rationale: Correcting a misleading classification in my own v1 map while the remaining source budget is available. The v1 Transport surface labelled net_transport.go, tcp_transport.go and inmem_transport.go as externalized on the grounds that the library 'does not implement the wire', but those three files are in-repository Transport implementations that this run never read. Caller injection of an interface does not externalize an unread in-repository implementation, so the surface is split: the in-repo implementations are kept as a deferred, unread library responsibility, and a separate externalized surface records the Transport interface contract the handlers actually assume.

target_profile.rationale: The selection_injection entry claimed the library 'neither opens sockets nor chooses durability', which is false for the shipped transport implementations: NewNetworkTransport and NewTCPTransport do own socket and connection handling. The entry now states which dependencies are always caller-injected and which the library also implements itself, and the target_profile unknowns record that those in-repo transports were not read in this run.

surface:Transport (net_transport.go, tcp.rationale: The disposition changes from externalized to deferred and the reason from a claim about the wire to the actual boundary: NetworkTransport, TCPTransport and InmemTransport are library code whose framing, connection lifecycle, heartbeat fast-path dispatch and pipeline semantics were not read, so their correctness is an open library responsibility. The behavior_ids are cleared because no behavior was mapped to these unread implementations, and the sources now point at the declarations that show the library ships them rather than citing the handler that merely assumes a transport.

feedback.answered: The v1 map misclassified the library's own transport implementations as externalized. net_transport.go (NetworkTransport, NewNetworkTransport and its variants), tcp_transport.go (NewTCPTransport and its variants) and inmem_transport.go (InmemTransport, NewInmemTransport) are in-repository implementations, so their delivery, ordering, connection and pipeline behaviour is a library responsibility that this run has not read; only the reliance of the protocol handlers on an injected Transport is externalized to whoever supplies one. The map now records both surfaces separately.
remaining: The three in-repo transport implementations remain unread: their message framing, connection handling, heartbeat fast-path dispatch, AppendEntriesPipeline ordering and in-process delivery semantics are unmapped responsibilities.

The same review has not been applied to the other externalized surfaces (FSM determinism and the durable stores); those remain correct as stated because the FSM and store implementations are genuinely caller-supplied, but that was not re-checked file by file here.

Reachability of the installSnapshot watermark case from a legal leader history, the compacted-leader variant of the truncation-failure case, and execution corroboration of the two reading-based consequences remain open.
feedback.rationale: This is a correction of an inaccurate boundary I introduced, not new protocol knowledge, and it is recorded with the sources that justify the corrected classification. It adds no obligation and does not change any requirement or confirmed result; the three in-repo transport files are preserved as an explicit unread surface instead of being absorbed into an externalized claim.
